## Verdict (headline)

**GAP 8 is genuinely fixed and confirmed live** (attempt 7's run-B killer). For the first time the
codex prover's decomposition was ACCEPTED by `af record-proof` (`record-proof-failed=0`,
`proof-recorded` fired), the forward-sibling `depends` bridge translated cleanly, and run B validated
real nodes — attempt 7's run B validated 0.

**Both directions produced dramatically LEANER, AISM-shaped trees than attempt 7** and validated their
full child frontier cross-vendor, but **both dead-ended at the SAME new wall: the ROOT conjecture (node

the operator's to fix (§7, "pick nothing silently"). Both runs terminated `stuck-no-progress` (3

## GAP 9 (both runs) — the ROOT node's author is the `af init` author (unparseable), so the cross-vendor apply gate fails closed on final root validation

### What happened (driver-log, verbatim)

Run A (`_logs/lem-weighted-min.run-A.driver-log.jsonl`) and run B
(`_logs/lem-weighted-min.run-B.driver-log.jsonl`), after all children validated and node `1` returned
to the verifier frontier:

Run A (×2):
```
{"kind":"cross-vendor-rejected","at":"2026-07-20T14:25:09.157Z","node":"1","reason":"identity-unparseable"}
{"kind":"node-skipped","at":"2026-07-20T14:25:09.157Z","node":"1","reason":"cross-vendor: identity-unparseable on load-bearing node '1' (prover=unknown, verifier=gpt) — fails closed, never conflated with a confirmed same-family violation"}
```
Run B (×1):
```
{"kind":"cross-vendor-rejected","at":"2026-07-20T14:31:15.337Z","node":"1","reason":"identity-unparseable"}
{"kind":"node-skipped","at":"2026-07-20T14:31:15.337Z","node":"1","reason":"cross-vendor: identity-unparseable on load-bearing node '1' (prover=unknown, verifier=claude) — fails closed, never conflated with a confirmed same-family violation"}
```

Then `stuck-no-progress` (3 rounds) in both. `bind-failed=0 parse-failed=0 record-proof-failed=0` in
both runs — the ONLY failure is the root's cross-vendor identity check.

### Root cause (confirmed from the af ledger)

- Every CHILD node carries a family-tagged prover author, stamped by `af record-proof`:
  run A children `author: claude|claude|claude-opus-4-8|claim-lem-weighted-min-prover`; run B children
  `author: gpt|codex|gpt-5.6-sol|claim-lem-weighted-min-prover`. Children validate cleanly cross-vendor
  (verified_by the OTHER family) — 8 in run A, 5 in run B.
- The ROOT node `1` was created by `af init -a "rk-m3.5-baseline-prep"` (runbook §4). Its `node.author`
  in the ledger is empty/None — NOT a family-tagged prover identity. `af record-proof` stamps the
  prover identity on the CHILDREN it creates, but does NOT update the PARENT's `author` to the prover
  that decomposed it. So the root's decomposition-prover identity is not recorded anywhere the
  cross-vendor apply gate reads.
- When node `1` returns to the verifier frontier for final validation, rk's apply-time cross-vendor
  check (PRD C9) reads node `1`'s `author` to determine the prover family, gets `unknown`
  (unparseable), and — correctly — **fails closed** rather than conflate an unparseable identity with a
  confirmed same-family violation. The verdict is rejected; the root never validates; 3 no-progress
  rounds → stuck.
- **The fail-closed behavior is CORRECT and intended.** The gap is that the root's prover-of-record is
  not propagated to where the gate looks — exactly the STOP-6/7/8 pattern one layer deeper: a
  structural producer/consumer mismatch surfacing only now that a tree fully decomposes AND its
  children all clear, letting the root reach final re-verification (attempt 7 never got here — GAP 8 or
  budget stopped it first).

### Why this is direction-independent

Both runs hit it identically (`prover=unknown` in both; only the verifier family differs, gpt vs
claude). It keys on the ROOT's own author, which is the init author regardless of which vendor
decomposed the tree. Any root created by `af init` (i.e. every baseline workspace, and every real
campaign root) is affected. This structurally blocks full-tree convergence for BOTH directions of the
current baseline until fixed.

### Escalation (L6 / §7)

Validity-semantic (cross-vendor apply gate + author/provenance) → Tier-A, top-tier review before any
fix lands. NOT fixed here. Fix options (for the owning triage, not decided here):
- (9a) rk-side: when `record-proof` decomposes node N, also record N's prover-of-record (the prover
  that authored the decomposition) in a field the cross-vendor gate reads for N's own validation —
  today it only reads `node.author`, which for a root is the init author.
- (9b) af-side (vibefeld): have `record-proof` set/update the parent's author to the recording
  prover, or expose a `proved_by` field distinct from `author`, so the decomposition-prover identity
  is first-class on the parent.
- (9c) semantic clarification: define, in `docs/verdicts-apply.md` / PRD C9, WHOSE family the
  cross-vendor rule compares for a node that was CONJECTURED by one party and DECOMPOSED (proved) by
  another — the verifier must differ from the prover-of-record, which for a decomposed node is the
  decomposer, not the original conjecture author.

- **cross-vendor prove→verify validated live, author + verified_by recorded:** YES, both directions

- **full-tree convergence (root validated AND closed) observed live:** **NO — NOT reached.** The root
  is `pending/unresolved` in both directions, blocked by GAP 9 (the cross-vendor apply gate fails
  closed on the root's unparseable author), NOT by rk-6nv's own prove→verify mechanism, which
  terminated correctly for every child node. rk-6nv's last open piece (root validated + closed live)
  remains open, now blocked by GAP 9 rather than GAP 8/budget. This is the SINGLE remaining obstacle to
  a fully-converged lemma, and it is well-isolated.
